context:
Please help me with the following task. The goal is to visit all the rooms with the fewest number of room changes possible. In each room, you need to decide the direction to go in. Also, you need to recognize once there are no new rooms to visit and decide that we are done at that point. Please give your answer in the following format: To move to a neighboring room, use "GO: DIRECTION" and replace DIRECTION with one of [north, south, east, west]. To stop the exploration, answer with "DONE" instead. Omit any other text.
Here is an example:
You are in the Kitchen. Currently available directions: south, west. What is your next instruction?
GO: west
You have made a step and entered a Lobby. Currently available directions: east, north. What is your next instruction?
GO: north
...
You have made a step and entered a Bedroom. Currently available directions: south. What is your next instruction?
DONE
Let us start. You are in the Conservatory. Currently available directions: south, north. What is your next instruction?

Next time, I would mentally map the layout, note visited rooms, and prioritize unexplored directions to systematically cover all rooms before stopping.
-
 I failed because I did not stop when all rooms were visited. I moved from Kitchen to Studio, which was likely a new room, but I should have tracked visited rooms and recognized when no new rooms remained. Next time, I would keep a mental map and stop when all directions lead to already-visited rooms.
-
 Failed. I got stuck in a loop between Exercise room and Bar because I only moved east/west without exploring other possible connections. I should have mapped visited rooms and avoided revisiting unless necessary to reach new areas. Next time, track visited rooms and prioritize unexplored directions to cover all rooms efficiently.
